In January 2027, her first $300,000 buys a ladder of Treasury bonds and funds with an end date, one rung falling due before each cheque.

Her 2028 deposit first finishes any rung the first $300,000 couldn't buy. The remainder, roughly the interest it should earn, goes into one world index fund, spread across thousands of companies. That is under a tenth of her money. Banks sell the same idea as a capital-protected note, but they spend that interest on an option, which expires worthless if the market stands still. Shares don't expire. We assume world shares earn about 7.5% a year over the long run, but the cheques never depend on it.
